messages:
Kai: Hey all — I'm Kai, started today in infra. Got a Dell XPS provisioned but Intune shows 'Device not compliant: BitLocker not enabled'. Tried to enable BitLocker and it prompts for TPM ownership/error. I don't have local admin. Need to install WSL + Docker so would prefer an admin elevation or a clear step-by-step to finish encryption. Any tips? cc @IT-Support :wave:

IT-Support: Hi Kai — welcome! :tada: We saw the device enroll attempt. Can you share the exact Intune error screenshot or paste the message? Also run this in PowerShell (admin if possible, but try normal first):

```
Get-BitLockerVolume -MountPoint C:\\
```

If that returns errors, run `manage-bde -status C:` from an elevated cmd. If TPM isn't owned you might see 'TPM not ready' or similar.

Kai: I can't run as admin yet — that's the problem. The portal shows a red compliance banner with: "BitLocker not enabled — user action required". I clicked "Enable BitLocker" and it failed with "TPM ownership required".

Sam: @Kai I've filed a short IT ticket on your behalf for temporary admin (expiring in 24h) so you can install dev tools. Ticket #IT-4821. If IT needs approval from Security we'll loop Jordan.

Jordan: Quick security note — we don't grant permanent local admin. We can do a 24-hour elevation or use our privileged uplift flow via Okta MFA. Kai, do you need admin to enable BitLocker, or can we do it remotely? If TPM needs clearing/ownership we'll need physical access or remote TPM clear via OEM tool.

Kai: I need admin to install WSL + Docker and to run the BitLocker enable flow. I'm remote in PST. I can be available for a remote session.

IT-Support: OK scheduling a remote session. Meanwhile, if you can open an elevated PowerShell during the session we'll run:

```
Enable-BitLocker -MountPoint "C:\\" -EncryptionMethod XtsAes256 -UsedSpaceOnly
```

If TPM ownership is the blocker we'll either clear TPM via BIOS/UEFI (Dell support) or use our agent to take ownership during enrollment.

Alex: FWIW for WSL+Docker we typically do this (post-admin):

```
# enable features
wsl --install -d ubuntu
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName VirtualMachinePlatform
Restart-Computer
# then install Docker Desktop (system install)
```

If BitLocker is on, Docker won't care. If you need Docker Desktop without admin later we can provide a dev container on a dedicated VM as a fallback.

Jordan: Kai, quick checklist for the remote session — 1) confirm BIOS TPM setting (fTPM on), 2) join device to AzureAD (should be auto), run `dsregcmd /status` to confirm; 3) run BitLocker enablement commands; 4) capture Recovery Key in Intune. We'll ensure Recovery Key escrow.

Kai: Got it. Screenshot attached in the ticket. Available at 3pm PST. Thanks everyone.

IT-Support: Scheduled remote session for 15:00 PST. You'll get a calendar invite with a remote assistance link. Please have the laptop plugged in and connected to VPN.

Sam: Welcome again @Kai — ping me if the remote session times out. Also send your preferred GitHub handle and Slack timezone so we can set you up in on-call rotas later. :slightly_smiling_face:

Kai: Session went well — IT took ownership of TPM and enabled BitLocker. Intune now shows compliant. They applied a 24-hour admin token so I installed WSL & Docker. All set. Thanks team! :rocket:
